title: Gym Nutrition Guide
meta_desc: Discover what to eat before and after the gym to boost performance and recovery. Get expert advice on timing, hydration, and simple NZ foods to fuel your fitness journey.
intro: As a gym-goer in New Zealand, it's essential to fuel your body with the right foods at the right time to get the most out of your workout. Proper nutrition can help improve performance, speed up recovery, and support your overall fitness goals. In this guide, we'll cover the basics of what to eat before and after the gym, as well as provide tips on hydration and simple NZ foods to support your training.

sections.heading: Timing is Everything
sections.body: When it comes to eating before the gym, timing is crucial. Aim to eat a balanced meal with a mix of complex carbohydrates, protein, and healthy fats 1-3 hours before your workout. This allows for proper digestion and energy release. For example, if you're planning a morning workout, try having a bowl of oatmeal with banana, honey, and almond butter around 7-8 am.
list: Eat a balanced meal 1-3 hours before your workout
Include complex carbohydrates, protein, and healthy fats
Avoid heavy meals close to your workout time

sections.heading: Pre-Workout Foods in NZ
sections.body: In New Zealand, you can easily find healthy pre-workout foods at your local supermarket or gym cafe. Some great options include bananas, apples, energy bars, and trail mix with nuts and dried fruits. Many NZ gyms, such as Les Mills and City Fitness, offer healthy snack options and meal plans to support your training.
list: Trail mix with nuts and dried fruits

sections.heading: Hydration in the NZ Climate
sections.body: Staying hydrated is essential, especially in New Zealand's climate. Aim to drink at least 8-10 glasses of water per day, and make sure to drink water before, during, and after your workout. You can also consume electrolyte-rich drinks, such as coconut water or sports drinks, to help replenish lost salts and minerals. Jetts and Anytime Fitness gyms often have water fountains and vending machines with healthy drink options.
list: Drink at least 8-10 glasses of water per day
Consume electrolyte-rich drinks during and after intense workouts
Avoid sugary drinks and caffeine close to your workout time

sections.heading: Post-Workout Nutrition
sections.body: After your workout, it's essential to refuel your body with a mix of carbohydrates and protein to support muscle recovery and growth. Aim to eat a balanced meal or snack within 30-60 minutes after your workout. Some great post-workout foods in NZ include protein shakes, Greek yogurt with berries, and wholegrain toast with avocado and eggs. Many NZ gyms, such as Les Mills and City Fitness, offer post-workout nutrition advice and meal plans to support your recovery.
list: Eat a balanced meal or snack within 30-60 minutes after your workout
Include a mix of carbohydrates and protein

sections.heading: Get Started with Your Fitness Journey
sections.body: Now that you know what to eat before and after the gym, it's time to get started with your fitness journey. Remember to stay hydrated, listen to your body, and fuel your workouts with the right foods. If you're looking for a gym that supports your training and nutrition needs, compare NZ gyms and find the best one for you.
